projects.title: Durbuy Adventure Valley
projects.intro: A themed outdoor zone at Adventure Valley in Durbuy — Wildwood and Wild Nest. One visual language, carved and built by hand, carried through every gate, sign, sculpture and building in the park.
steps: The work is spread across a whole outdoor zone. Every element stands in the weather, gets touched by thousands of visitors a day, and has to look like it grew where it stands.
Concept Factory set a single visual language for the zone: carved lettering, weathered timber, colour taken from the forest. Every gate and marker speaks it.
Signs, arches and sculptures are cut, carved and painted by hand in the atelier. Nothing here is a printed panel screwed to a post.
A zone that reads as one world from the entrance arch to the last marker on the trail.

projects.title: Rose's Mystery House
projects.intro: A complete themed venue in the centre of Bucharest — a gothic house built inside a building, a botanical bar around it, characters and walk-through spaces. Designed in Herentals, built on site.
steps: A bare commercial space in Bucharest had to become a finished themed venue, drawn in Belgium and built on location with a local crew.
Rather than dressing the walls, Concept Factory built a full gothic facade indoors, with lit windows and a cobbled street in front of it. Guests walk up to a house that is not there.
The venue is dressed and then inhabited: figures, props and costumes made in-house, worn by performers who belong to the set.
A world guests step into straight off the street.

projects.title: Zeg Eens Euh
projects.intro: A studio set for the Play4 programme Zeg Eens Euh — a wall of lit panels, a curved desk and an audience floor, built in the atelier and installed in the studio.
steps: A set that reads on camera
Shapes and colour strong enough to hold up under studio light and from every camera position, delivered on a broadcast schedule.
A wall of individually lit panels gives the studio depth and lets lighting change the mood between rounds.
The desk is a curved ribbed shell with integrated light, machined and assembled in-house.
A complete studio world with the audience in it, handed over ready to shoot.

projects.title: Durbuy — Escape Rooms
projects.intro: Escape rooms at Adventure Valley, each one its own world: an emergency bunker on a countdown, a collapsed mine, a collector’s study and a room where the walls hold the clues.
steps: Rooms that share walls and services but have to feel like different places the moment the door closes.
Each room gets its own period, palette and light. Nothing is shared between them except the corridor.
The plot is carried by the build: days counted in tally marks on the wall, ration tins on a shelf, paperwork aged by hand.
Rooms that hold up under a torch beam and a group in a hurry.

projects.title: Rose's Mystery House — Escape Rooms
projects.intro: The escape rooms inside Rose’s Mystery House — a gothic run of spaces from a panelled parlour to a crypt, a library with a hidden passage and a corridor of stone.
steps: Dark, dense rooms that still have to be safe, navigable and reset in minutes between groups.
Rock, tombstones and walls sculpted in relief, so every surface holds up when a torch is held against it.
Cabinets, clocks, maps and paperwork aged by hand until nothing in the room looks bought.
Rooms a character can walk into, with a story that runs across the whole venue.

projects.title: Napoleon
projects.intro: An open-air stage world for Historalia’s Napoleon — a monumental scenography built in a castle park, playing to a full house every night of the run.
steps: The stage is a castle park. Everything has to be built on site, survive weeks of open air, and still read from the back row of a temporary grandstand.
Cannon wheels, giant laurel leaves and rearing horses set the scale before a single word is spoken. The castle itself stays in the frame as part of the decor.
The covered stage structure goes up first, then the scenery is built into it — a full construction site before it becomes a theatre.
A set that carries a cast of over a hundred and holds an audience from dusk into the dark.

projects.title: Slagharen Parade
projects.intro: A western parade for Slagharen — a convoy of weathered timber and rusted metal that has to look a century old and drive through the park every day of the season.
steps: Floats that read as antique but are road-safe, light enough to tow and stable with performers on board.
Each float is its own scene — a loaded cargo wagon, a delivery truck, a stand — reading together as one caravan.
Timber, metal and paint aged by hand, with a finish built to survive a full outdoor season.
A parade that runs through the park every day it is open.

projects.title: De Muizenval
projects.intro: A complete Gothic stage environment for Backstage Producties — designed, engineered and built in-house, from the first blueprint to the final reveal under the lights.
steps: A whole world, on a deadline
A believable Gothic interior, rich enough for the back row, light enough to move, ready for a hard opening night.
The director's mood translated into a spatial concept, then into technical drawings the workshop could build to the millimetre.
Every panel, moulding and piece of furniture machined, sculpted and scenic-painted by hand.
Installed on site for opening night — a single, coherent world the cast could live in.

projects.title: Aspe — Club Paparazzi
projects.intro: A nightclub built for the stage. For the theatre production Aspe, Concept Factory built a complete club interior that has to read from the back row under theatre lighting, and hold up for the length of a run.
steps: A club that reads from row 20
On stage a nightclub has to be legible at distance and under theatre light, and it has to be built so a crew can set it up and strike it without damage.
The space was designed around its lighting. Lasers, practicals and LED are part of the build rather than something aimed at it afterwards.
A complete club world on stage, delivered for the production schedule.

projects.title: Lijn 3
projects.intro: A large open-air stage set for the production Lijn 3 — Concept Factory took care of the scenic design and supported the build, turning a full street of house fronts into a playable stage.
steps: A whole street, under the open sky
An outdoor stage asks for a set that reads from far back, survives the weather and still gives the cast doors, windows and levels to play with.
Concept Factory developed the scenic design for the production — the street, the facades and the way the scenes move through them.
Technical support during the realisation, from drawings and detailing to on-site follow-up.
A full street as a stage — lit at night, played from front to back, with the ensemble using every facade.
